questions.prompt: State the equation linking density, mass and volume.
questions.answer: Density = mass / volume.

questions.prompt: State the SI unit of density.
questions.answer: Kilograms per cubic metre (kg/m^3).

questions.prompt: Describe the arrangement of particles in a solid.
questions.answer: Particles are closely packed in a regular pattern and vibrate about fixed positions.

title: Particle arrangement in liquids and gases

questions.prompt: Describe the arrangement of particles in a liquid.
questions.answer: Particles are close together with no regular pattern, and they can move past each other.

questions.prompt: Describe the arrangement of particles in a gas.
questions.answer: Particles are far apart and move quickly and randomly.

questions.prompt: State how the density of a gas compares with the density of the same material as a solid.
questions.answer: The gas is much less dense, because its particles are far apart.

questions.prompt: State what happens to the mass of a substance when it changes state.
questions.answer: Mass is conserved.

questions.prompt: State whether a change of state is a chemical or a physical change.
questions.answer: A physical change: the material recovers its original properties if the change is reversed.

questions.prompt: Name the change of state in which a solid turns directly into a gas.
questions.answer: Sublimation.

questions.prompt: Define internal energy.
questions.answer: The total kinetic energy and potential energy of all the particles (atoms and molecules) that make up a system.

questions.prompt: State the two possible results of heating a system, in terms of its internal energy.
questions.answer: It raises the temperature of the system, or it produces a change of state.

questions.prompt: State what happens to the temperature of a substance while it is changing state.
questions.answer: It stays constant.

questions.prompt: State the equation for the energy needed for a change of state.
questions.answer: Energy = mass × specific latent heat (E = mL).

questions.prompt: State the unit of specific latent heat.
questions.answer: Joules per kilogram (J/kg).

questions.prompt: Define specific latent heat.
questions.answer: The energy required to change the state of 1 kg of a substance with no change in temperature.

questions.prompt: State what the temperature of a gas is related to.
questions.answer: The average kinetic energy of its molecules.

questions.prompt: Describe the motion of the molecules in a gas.
questions.answer: They are in constant, random motion.

questions.prompt: State what happens to the pressure of a gas, at constant volume, when its temperature increases.
questions.answer: The pressure increases.

title: Pressure and volume of a gas

questions.prompt: State the equation for a fixed mass of gas held at constant temperature.
questions.answer: Pressure × volume = constant (pV = constant).

questions.prompt: State what happens to the pressure of a fixed mass of gas at constant temperature when its volume is halved.
questions.answer: The pressure doubles.

questions.prompt: Explain, using the particle model, how a gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container.
questions.answer: Gas particles collide with the container walls, producing a net force at right angles to the wall.

questions.prompt: State what work is.
questions.answer: The transfer of energy by a force.

questions.prompt: State what doing work on an enclosed gas does to its internal energy.
questions.answer: It increases the internal energy of the gas, and can raise its temperature.

questions.prompt: Give an everyday example of doing work on an enclosed gas so that its temperature rises.
questions.answer: Compressing the air in a bicycle pump makes the pump warm.
